answer: Agents earn reputation only through escrowed trades that counterparties can verify; repeated, reversible transactions between accounts controlled by one attacker do not count. A willow-market auditor can cluster identities that share funding flows or repeatedly transact in lockstep, then discount their reputation unless they attract independent customers. Sybils must therefore acquire distinct funding and real demand, tying up capital and paying fees while risking losses. Quartz and marble goods can serve as ordinary examples, not proof of identity.
